From Wiktionary, the free dictionary
See also: Appendix:Variations of "pina"

English

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Spanish piña.

Noun

[edit]

piña (countable and uncountable, plural piñas)

  1. cloth woven from pineapple fiber
  2. (metalworking) A cone of silver amalgam prepared for retorting.
  3. (metalworking) The residual cone of spongy silver left after the retorting.

Translations

[edit]
cloth
  • Finnish: ananashamppu

Anagrams

[edit]
  • APNI, NIPA, PAIN, PANI, Pain, nipa, pain, pian

Galician

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • pinha (reintegrationist)

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese, from Latin pīnea.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈpiɲa/ [ˈpi.ɲɐ]
  • Rhymes: -iɲa
  • Hyphenation: pi‧ña

Noun

[edit]

piña f (plural piñas)

  1. pinecone
  2. pineapple
  3. bunch (of grapes)
    Synonyms: acio, cacho

Derived terms

[edit]
  • piñeiro

References

[edit]
  • Seoane, Ernesto Xosé González; Granja, María Álvarez de la; Agrelo, Ana Isabel Boullón (2006–2022), “piña”, in Dicionario de Dicionarios do galego medieval [Dictionary of dictionaries of Medieval Galician] (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega
  • Antón Luís Santamarina Fernández, Ernesto Xosé González Seoane, María Álvarez de la Granja, editors (2003–2018), “piña”, in Tesouro informatizado da lingua galega (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega
  • Rosario Álvarez Blanco, editor (2014–2024), “piña”, in Tesouro do léxico patrimonial galego e portugués (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega, →ISSN
  • “piña”, in Dicionario da Real Academia Galega (in Galician), A Coruña: Royal Galician Academy, 2012–2026

Spanish

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈpiɲa/ [ˈpi.ɲa]
  • Audio (Colombia):(file)
  • Rhymes: -iɲa
  • Syllabification: pi‧ña

Etymology 1

[edit]

Inherited from Latin pīnea. The sense "pineapple" comes from its resemblance to a pinecone, similarly to English pineapple. The sense "core of the agave plant" comes from its resemblance to a pineapple after the leaves are chopped off for harvesting.

Noun

[edit]

piña f (plural piñas)

  1. (botany) pinecone
    Synonyms: estróbilo, cono
  2. pineapple
    Synonyms: ananá (Argentina, Uruguay), ananás
  3. (figurative) close-knit group
    • 2020 April 10, Los Desayunos de TVE (television production), Pablo Iglesias Turrión (actor):
      […] debatimos de muchas cosas, pero una vez que las cosas se debaten, y una vez que llegamos a un acuerdo, somos una piña
      (please add an English translation of this quotation)
  4. the core of the agave plant
  5. (El Salvador, colloquial) gay male
  6. (Peru, colloquial) bad luck
Derived terms
[edit]
  • apiñar
  • piña colada
  • piñal
  • piñata
  • piñazo
  • piñón
Related terms
[edit]
  • pino
Descendants
[edit]
  • → English: piña
  • → Central Bikol: pinya
  • → Cebuano: pinya
  • → Hiligaynon: pinya
  • → Tagalog: pinya

Etymology 2

[edit]

Back-formation from piñata.

Noun

[edit]

piña f (plural piñas)

  1. (Canary Islands, Rioplatense, Venezuela, Bolivia, Paraguay, Honduras, Cuba) a punch
    Synonym: puñetazo
    1. (Dominican Republic, Argentina) fight
  2. (Argentina, colloquial) collision, accident, crash
